analysis:
Examined the new offline requantizer scripts/models/requant.py, the hash-pinned requirements file and the metadata of test_model_requant_upload.py; the test file's source was not supplied.

requant.py range-reads a template (models.darkbloom.ai) and a bf16 source (a Hugging Face resolve URL pinned to a sha). It re-quantizes the linear layers with numpy and writes shards plus config, index and the copied files.

- Range reads enforce exact length (lines 39-58). That avoids silently using a whole-object 200 response, but there is no digest check on source or template bytes. Integrity rests on HTTPS plus the pinned HF revision, and on the canonical manifest of the output (docstring line 21).
- An integrity gap exists for model weights: a tampered input produces an output whose hash still verifies (A-004, T-012, T-027). The weight hash attests only the output, not provenance from the source.
- Finding: unconfined manifest paths are written at lines 401-407.
- requirements-requant-upload.txt pins every package with --require-hashes and --only-binary, which is a supply-chain improvement. I could not verify that the hashes are genuine.
- No provider runtime, coordinator or attestation code changed. TB-002, TB-009 and TB-011 are not affected.

Integration must examine the following, none of which were in this batch:
- .github/workflows/model-requant-upload.yml: how --template and --source are chosen, whether inputs are validated, and how credentials are scoped and masked.
- upload-model-revision.py: manifest validation and whether the canonical manifest is compared before publishing.
- Whether the output directory sits in a location where overwritten files are executed later.

findings.detail: At scripts/models/requant.py lines 401-407 (head), cmd_build reads manifest.json from the template URL. It then writes every listed path with open(os.path.join(a.out, p), 'wb'). p is not normalized or rejected when absolute or when it contains '..', and os.path.join discards a.out when p is absolute. Trigger: a tampered or wrongly selected template prefix, or an operator-supplied --template URL pointing at a host they do not control, lists a path such as '../../.github/...' or '/home/runner/...'. Impact: arbitrary file write on the build host or CI runner. If the upload workflow holds R2 credentials (A-004 publication path), the next step could run the overwritten file and tamper with what gets uploaded. This matters because providers serve whatever revision is uploaded (T-012/T-027 class). The same unvalidated names reach the URLs built at lines 98 and 405 and the weight_map. Fix: accept only relative, normalized basenames matching an allowlist pattern, with no '/', '..' or absolute paths. Check os.path.realpath(dest) stays under a.out. Optionally verify each copied file's sha256 against the manifest entry before writing.
findings.title: build writes template-manifest paths without confining them to the output directory
